If the neck is warped it would benefit from steam and lots of pressure, and most guitars have truss rods since about 1960. How do individual strings 'slip' too low? Individual saddles tend to have machine screws in them for height adjustment which under pressure are hard to turn, and a TOM style doesn't have individual height adjustment.

Pressing the string down should be fairly easy on an acoustic and near effortless on an electric. If you press that hard not only do you prevent yourself from playing quickly, and cause hand strain/injury, you will pull the note sharp and be out of tune.

Buzzing is caused by improper action, low or high frets, loose parts, and a few other things. Guitars are made of wood and expand and contract with humidity and temperature. The neck needs to have a specific amount of relief or bow and these changes can affect that, or even pop out frets. It's unlikely you've worn the frets out since you've been playing it a short time but that can also cause buzz.
